subject: Econ offset & go-live risk assessment for HyperData
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@hyperdata.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, HyperData Procurement <procurement@hyperdata.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Econ offset + go-live risk questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. We’re pulling together the internal business case and there are two things blocking approval: (1) migration/go-live risk (esp. data egress and runtime parity) and (2) the economics vs our incumbent (they’re offering multi-quarter credits + a 20% volume rebate).

Before we jump into redlines I wanted to ask roughly what you can do on the economics side for a first-year go-live: are there migration credits or onboarding discounts you typically offer for a customer of our size? Also, any guarantees around runtime parity (latency percentiles) and a playbook if we see quality regressions post-cutover?

We’re aiming to make a recommendation to the execs by 30 Jun. If you can send a short, skimmable counteroffer matrix that shows incremental concessions + operational mitigations, that’d help speed things up.

Cheers,
Morgan
Head of AI Platforms
HyperData

Attachment: incumbent-offer-summary.xlsx (referenced)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@hyperdata.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 12:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ offset + go-live risk questions

Morgan — thank you, and appreciate the clear ask + deadline.

High level: we can structure a targeted offer that addresses both cost parity and operational risk. I’ve put three options below (short summary for execs first, details after). I’m attaching a one-pager and an SOW draft for the integration scope.

Executive summary (pick one):
- Option A — Accelerated Onboard: 10% first-year runtime discount + $120k migration credit (applied over Q1) + 3 months premium support for free.
- Option B — Risk-Shared Pilot: No upfront credit, but 6-week pilot with a service-level rollback clause and a $75k contingent credit if SLA targets missed. If pilot succeeds, 12% year-one discount.
- Option C — Term Commitment: 18-month commit with 15% discount, $60k onboarding credit, and a dedicated migration engineer for first 90 days.

Operational mitigations we’ll include regardless of option:
- Model parity checklist and pre-cutover benchmark suite run against your QPS and 95th/99th latency windows.
- KV cache warm-up plan + prefix caching to reduce cold-start variance.
- Fallback routing to read-only variant and automatic throttling thresholds to protect latency SLOs.
- Quarterly evals for 6 months with rollback playbook and cross-functional runbook shared.

Attachments: HyperData-Migration-Offer-v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB); SOW-draft-HyperData.docx (DOCX, 55KB). Also included a CSV with the credit matrix.

If you’re open, I recommend Option A as the fastest path to approval; it pairs immediate economic relief with a clear onboarding credit and support band.

I’ll be available this afternoon to hop on 20–30 min to walk exec-level slides.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
From: Alex Chang <alex.chang@hyperdata.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@hyperdata.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Econ offset + go-live risk questions

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions from finance: 
1) How is the $120k migration credit in Option A delivered (invoice credit, usage rebate, or applied as professional services credit)?
2) For Option C, what are the volume tiers that determine the 15% discount? We need breakpoints to model FY28 spend.

Also — our CFO will want to see the worst-case exposure if we sign and then need to roll back in 90 days. If you have a short note on liability or termination economics (and whether Redwood would pay for a portion of re-implementation costs) that’d be very helpful.

Regards,
Alex
VP Finance, HyperData

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: HyperData concession plan and exposure

Sofia/Laura — quick internal note before we reply to Alex:

- Delivery mechanism: migration credit should be a credit memo applied to usage invoices over quarter 1 (reduces cash flow hit and keeps bookkeeping clean). Avoid one-off checks.
- Liability exposure: we do not offer to fund customer re-implementation costs normally. Instead propose an SLA contingent credit (cap the credit at 25% of Q1 committed spend) and include a shared post-mortem with our SREs and their infra team.
- Volume breakpoints for Option C: 0–4M tokens/month (base rate), 4–12M tokens/month (-10% additional), >12M tokens/month (-15% additional). These are conservative but defensible.
- We should also offer a 60-day rollback window with tech support and a reduced offboarding fee if rollback is initiated within that window.

I’ll draft a short reply that answers Alex directly and frames the credit as usage rebated so our treasury is neutral.

Jordan
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Econ offset + go-live risk questions — formal offer

Morgan / Alex — attaching a short offer that implements the points below. Per Alex’s ask:
- Option A delivery: $120k delivered as a usage credit (applied over Q1 invoices) so net cash impact to you is immediate but bookkeeping straightforward.
- Option C tiers: base (0–4M tokens/mo), 4–12M (-10%), >12M (-15%). We will include a schedule in the agreement.
- Rollback economics: 60-day rollback window; SLA-contingent credits capped at 25% of committed Q1 spend. We will not fund re-implementation directly, but will provide a dedicated post-mortem and transition engineer at reduced rate.

Next steps: I’ve attached the updated offer (HyperData-Migration-Offer-v3.pdf) and a draft SOW. If that looks good, I can send a DocuSign envelope for the commercial term sheet and we’ll open a HubSpot PO record.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HD-8721) | DocuSign (https://docusign.com/envelope/0A12BCD3E45F)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call to run the exec summary.

Best,
Sofia
